newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission probes own security contract. [CORRECTED 16:44 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU Commission probes own security contract. [CORRECTED 16:44 GMT]

text.p: The European Commission is to probe a press allegation of malpractice in relation to a contract to provide security guards for the EU executive's buildings, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
Joao Vale de Almeida, commenting on a story in the Belgian Dutch-language newspaper De Morgen on Monday (corrects from Tuesday), said the Commission would look into various charges made.
"We note the allegations and take them very seriously. Some of them are very serious allegations... and certainly deserve the Commission's attention," he told a news conference.

His remarks referred to the Commission's contract with Group Four Securitas, which De Morgen said was worth 600 million francs ($16 million) a year from November 1992 to October this year, to provide 600 guards for all its buildings.
De Morgen alleged that Group Four Securitas won the contract using inside information and that irregularities in the agreement meant that some guards were overpaid.
Vale de Almeida said early problems related to the contract had been sorted out while routine Commission checks to date had yielded nothing to back up the paper's claims.
"Following such internal monitoring and inspections, we have never found any evidence of fraud or corruption involving Commission officials.
A spokesman for the Dutch-based company, who asked not to be named, told Reuters by telephone that there was no evidence to support the allegations, which he said were "overstated".
He said the charges, which dated from 1995, had been dealt with to the Commission's satisfaction.
"When we looked carefully at the allegations there were some matters we were unhappy about and we took appropriate action immediately."
This involved talks with the Commission and people being "relieved of their functions", he said.
"I'm not suggesting for one minute that there has been any fraudulent behaviour... the Commission is entirely happy with the service we provide," he said, refusing to give further detail.
